title: listener: verified loudness measures, conformance fixtures and a benchmark of published loudness phenomena for sound effects
description:
listener supports research on how loud sound effects are heard. No published study tests a loudness measure against listeners on sound effects, and the standard measures part by many dB where effects live: short, low, or with long tails.

It computes ITU-R BS.1770 (integrated, maximum momentary and short-term loudness, true peak), ISO 532-1 (maximum and N5), DIN 45692 sharpness and ECMA-418-2 (loudness, tonality, roughness) per file and per sound event at stated playback levels; checks them against EBU Tech 3341 and 3342, ISO 532-1 Annex B, DIN 45692 and the tones that define each unit; reports where the measures disagree on a corpus in dB of gain, to choose listening-test stimuli; and scores every measure against eleven published results on the loudness of short and changing sounds.

The release holds the results of the first run on 56 CC0 sound effects, a draft protocol for a loudness-matching test, and the plan for an event-level loudness model fitted to its data. Python 3.11 or later.
notes: Test signals and reference values of ISO 532-1, DIN 45692 and the EBU loudness test set are not included, nor is third-party audio: the 56 CC0 Sonic Pi samples are fetched as described in docs/FIRST_CHECKS.md. ECMA-418-2 comes from a separately licensed tool run as its own process (external/README.md).
